proposals: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should introduce the PNGRB Act amendment needed for the regulator to issue binding hydrogen transport and blending rules, with a published timeline, so that the drafting reported in September 2025 has a checkable end point.

PNGRB should publish a register of every approved hydrogen-blending trial, listing the operator, network type, approved blend percentage, approval date and each subsequent revision, so that the approved envelope is not reconstructed from company press releases and trade coverage.

PESO should publish the technical basis for each stage-wise blend approval — such as Indore’s step from 1.1% to 2.0% — including pipe material and test results, so that an India-specific evidence base replaces reliance on international reference points like NaturalHy and HyDeploy.

PNGRB should publish the final report of its World Bank-backed hydrogen transmission pathways study, including the technical-compatibility assessment, so that any national blend ceiling it later sets can be traced to Indian pipeline data rather than to a GAIL engineering presentation.

PNGRB should publish periodic performance results from the Indore, Surat and Ahmedabad pilots, covering leaks, metering accuracy and appliance complaints, since this post found no independent technical audit of any pilot’s results.
